ideas.pitch: A hardware-in-the-loop dashboard that visualizes a Micromouse robot's internal Flood Fill algorithm state and sensor telemetry over a high-speed serial link in real time.
ideas.title: FloodFill-Visualizer: Real-Time Maze Mapping & Path Optimization
ideas.why_it_could_win: Addresses the core technical challenge of Micromouse competitions—debugging and optimizing search algorithms—while providing a live, working demo that judges can watch in real-time.

ideas.pitch: A rapid prototyping and simulation tool for Micromouse teams to test turn-rate PID loops and search heuristics on virtual 16x16 mazes before burning code to physical hardware.
ideas.title: WallHugger-Sim: Hardware-in-the-Loop Micromouse Simulator
ideas.why_it_could_win: Solves the primary bottleneck of robot hacking: hardware breakages and lack of test tracks. A robust simulation tool enables safer, faster iteration under tight hackathon timeframes.

ideas.pitch: A companion calibration station that uses optical gates and IMU telemetry logging to auto-tune motor PWM limits and sensor thresholds for precise cell-to-cell navigation.
ideas.title: MicroScan: Inertial & IR Calibration Rig for Micromouse
ideas.why_it_could_win: Focuses on rigorous engineering precision and tuning, which directly translates to winning runs in speed-run phases of Micromouse tournaments.

ideas.pitch: An ultra-lightweight onboard data logger utilizing SPI flash to record microsecond-level encoder counts, gyro rates, and wall-sensor states during high-speed maze runs.
ideas.title: SpeedRun-Telemetry: Black Box Flight Recorder for Micromouse
ideas.why_it_could_win: Provides judges with hard, empirical proof of algorithmic optimization and hardware reliability during post-run analysis, separating elite robots from struggling prototypes.

ideas.pitch: A desktop utility that generates valid competition-standard 16x16 mazes and exports wall layout configurations directly to robot EEPROM over Bluetooth.
ideas.title: MazeGen: Automated 16x16 Maze Validator and Configurator
ideas.why_it_could_win: Addresses the practical infrastructure needs of running and testing against diverse maze configurations during a high-stakes robotics event.
